title: BNSS, JJ & Probation
sub: BNSS 2023 (old CrPC) · Juvenile Justice Act 2015 · Probation of Offenders Act 1958 · Osmania LLB (3 YDC) Sem V
journey: A crime is reported to the police, the accused is arrested and seeks bail, faces a fair trial, gets a verdict — and may still be reformed on probation; a child takes the separate Juvenile line.

stations.name: Why procedure?
stations.one: Substantive law says what a crime is; procedure says how to find, try and punish — fairly.
stations.boss: Maneka Gandhi v Union of India (1978) — procedure must be just, fair, reasonable

stations.name: Police, PP & defence
stations.one: Police investigate, the Public Prosecutor prosecutes fairly, defence counsel guards the accused.
stations.boss: Prakash Singh v Union of India (2006) — police reforms

stations.name: Kinds of offences
stations.one: Cognizable (police act without warrant) or not; bailable or not; warrant case = over 2 years.
stations.hook: C = Cop can act · N = Needs a Magistrate

stations.name: Criminal courts
stations.one: Sessions Court (any sentence, death needs HC), CJM (7 yrs), JMFC (3 yrs + ₹50,000), Executive Magistrate (order).

stations.name: FIR
stations.one: First information of a cognizable offence to the police — must be registered; Zero FIR, e-FIR.
stations.boss: Lalita Kumari v Govt of UP (2014) — registration is mandatory

stations.name: Investigation
stations.one: Spot visit, statements, seizure, forensics, inquest — ending in the police report (charge sheet).
stations.boss: Sakiri Vasu v State of UP (2008) — Magistrate can monitor investigation

stations.name: Arrest
stations.one: Without warrant for cognizable offences; up to 7 years — notice first, arrest only if necessary.
stations.boss: Arnesh Kumar v State of Bihar (2014) — no automatic arrest

stations.name: Process & absconders
stations.one: Summons → warrant → proclamation (30 days) → attachment → trial in absentia.

stations.name: CLA 2018
stations.one: Harsher rape punishments; probes and trials in 2 months; no anticipatory bail for rape of a girl under 16.
stations.hook: 2 m probe · 2 m trial · 6 m appeal

stations.name: Rights of the arrested
stations.one: Told the grounds, relative informed, lawyer, medical check, before a Magistrate in 24 hours.
stations.boss: D.K. Basu v State of West Bengal (1997) — 11 arrest safeguards

stations.name: Remand & default bail
stations.one: Police custody max 15 days (in parts); charge sheet late after 60/90 days → bail as of right.
stations.boss: M. Ravindran v DRI (2020) — default bail is indefeasible
stations.hook: Charge sheet late → bail by right

stations.name: Search & seizure
stations.one: With warrant or by police with written reasons, two witnesses, list, video.
stations.boss: M.P. Sharma v Satish Chandra (1954) — search ≠ self-incrimination

stations.name: Public order (old 144)
stations.one: Executive Magistrate’s urgent order to prevent danger; 2 months, extendable to 6.
stations.boss: Madhu Limaye v SDM Monghyr (1970) — preventive, reasonable restriction

stations.name: Complaint & dismissal
stations.one: Complaint to a Magistrate; complainant examined on oath; process issued or complaint dismissed.

stations.name: Bail
stations.one: Bailable → bail is a right; non-bailable → court’s discretion (woman, sick, under 16 favoured).
stations.boss: Satender Kumar Antil v CBI (2022) — bail is the rule, jail the exception

stations.name: Anticipatory bail
stations.one: Bail in advance from Sessions / HC for a person who fears arrest for a non-bailable offence.
stations.boss: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v State of Punjab (1980) — read liberally

stations.name: Bonds & cancellation
stations.one: No excessive bail; under-trials freed after half (first offenders ⅓) of the maximum; bail cancelled for misuse.
stations.boss: Dolat Ram v State of Haryana (1995) — grounds to cancel bail

stations.name: Fair trial
stations.one: Impartial judge, open court, lawyer, evidence in the accused’s presence, chance to explain.
stations.boss: Zahira Habibullah Sheikh (Best Bakery, 2004) — retrial outside Gujarat
stations.hook: Fair to accused, victim and society

stations.name: Presumption of innocence
stations.one: The prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
stations.boss: Kali Ram v State of HP (1973) — two views → accused wins

stations.name: Rights of accused & legal aid
stations.one: Lawyer of choice, free legal aid, silence, copies, cross-examination.
stations.boss: Suk Das v UT of Arunachal Pradesh (1986) — no legal aid, no valid trial

stations.name: Speedy trial
stations.one: Part of Art. 21; delay judged by length, reason and prejudice.
stations.boss: Hussainara Khatoon v State of Bihar (1979) — under-trials freed

stations.name: Venue, jurisdiction & limitation
stations.one: Tried where the offence happened; minor offences have time limits for cognizance (6 m / 1 yr / 3 yrs).
stations.boss: Sarah Mathew v Institute of Cardio Vascular Diseases (2014)

stations.name: Double jeopardy
stations.one: No second trial for the same offence or on the same facts after conviction / acquittal.
stations.boss: Maqbool Hussain v State of Bombay (1953) — needs prosecution + punishment

stations.name: Charge
stations.one: Written accusation: offence, section, time, place, person; separate charges with 5 exceptions.
stations.boss: Willie Slaney v State of MP (1956) — defect fatal only if prejudice

stations.name: Sessions trial
stations.one: Committal → discharge? → charge → evidence → accused heard → defence → judgment → sentence hearing.
stations.boss: Bachan Singh v State of Punjab (1980) — sentence hearing matters

stations.name: Warrant & summons trials
stations.one: Warrant case: formal charge and discharge stage; summons case: particulars only.

stations.name: Compounding
stations.one: Victim settles listed offences — the accused is acquitted.
stations.boss: Gian Singh v State of Punjab (2012) — HC may quash on settlement

stations.name: Plea bargaining
stations.one: Guilty plea for a lighter sentence + victim compensation; only up to 7 years; not for crimes against women / children.

stations.name: Summary trial
stations.one: Petty offences tried with a short record; theft up to ₹20,000; max 3 months.
stations.hook: Small case · short record · 3 months max

stations.name: Judgment & copies
stations.one: Points, decision, reasons; special reasons for death; free copy to the accused.

stations.name: Death & execution
stations.one: A Sessions death sentence waits for High Court confirmation; pregnant woman → life.
stations.boss: Bachan Singh v State of Punjab (1980) — rarest of rare
stations.hook: Death needs the High Court’s yes

stations.name: Release instead of sentence
stations.one: Convicted, but released after admonition or on probation of good conduct.

stations.name: Appeal, reference, revision
stations.one: Appeal is a statutory right; reference asks the HC a legal question; revision checks legality; no review.
stations.boss: Amar Nath v State of Haryana (1977) — no revision of interlocutory orders
stations.hook: Appeal = right · revision = check · review = no

stations.name: Victim & compensation
stations.one: Victim can be heard, appeal and be compensated — by the offender or the State scheme.
stations.boss: Ankush Shivaji Gaikwad v Maharashtra (2013) — always consider compensation
stations.hook: Offender pays — or the State does

stations.name: Probation
stations.one: Released on a good-conduct bond, under supervision, instead of jail.
stations.boss: Jugal Kishore Prasad v State of Bihar (1972) — keep first offenders out of jail

stations.name: Admonition
stations.one: Minor offences (≤ 2 years, theft, cheating) by a first offender — a warning is enough.

stations.name: Offenders under 21
stations.one: No imprisonment for under-21s unless the court records reasons.
stations.boss: Ishar Das v State of Punjab (1972) — overrides minimum sentence

stations.name: Probation officer
stations.one: Inquires and reports, supervises, advises and helps find work.

stations.name: Parole & furlough
stations.one: Executive’s temporary release of a convict — parole for a reason, furlough as routine.
stations.boss: Asfaq v State of Rajasthan (2017) — parole v furlough

stations.name: Remission & release
stations.one: Government may suspend, remit or commute sentences — 14-year floor for some life convicts.
stations.boss: Union of India v V. Sriharan (2016)

stations.name: Who is a child?
stations.one: Below 18 on the date of the offence; age proved by school / birth certificate, then medical test.
stations.boss: Pratap Singh v State of Jharkhand (2005) — date of offence decides

stations.name: Doli incapax
stations.one: Under 7 → no offence; 7–12 → no offence unless mature enough to understand.

stations.name: Juvenile Justice Board
stations.one: Magistrate + 2 social workers (one woman); sole forum for children in conflict with law.

stations.name: Bail & inquiry
stations.one: A child shall get bail unless it harms him; never in a lock-up; inquiry in 4 months.
stations.hook: Bail is the rule · lock-up never

stations.name: Heinous offence, 16–18
stations.one: Preliminary assessment; Children’s Court may try as adult — but no death, no life without release.
stations.boss: Subramanian Swamy v Raju (2014) — 18 stays the line

stations.name: Homes & rehabilitation
stations.one: Observation home, special home, place of safety; foster care, sponsorship, after-care.

stations.name: CWC & adoption
stations.one: Child Welfare Committee for children in need of care; adoption through CARA / DM.

stations.name: JJ Act — key features
stations.one: Child-first principles (S.3), JJB, CWC, no jail, fresh start, adult trial only for 16–18 heinous.
stations.boss: Sheela Barse v Union of India (1986) — children not in jails

xfer: every arrest switches on the rights of the arrested
FIR goes to the police; a complaint goes to the Magistrate
an acquittal can’t be retried — the State must appeal
no anticipatory bail for rape of a girl under 16 (CLA 2018)
release after conviction = probation under the PO Act
a child gets bail even in a non-bailable offence

routes.title: Can the police arrest him?
steps: Is the offence cognizable?
no
Only on a Magistrate’s warrant (S.72) — except refusal to give name and address (S.39).
Is it punishable up to 7 years, and is arrest not really necessary?
yes
Issue a notice of appearance (S.35(3)); arrest only with recorded reasons (Arnesh Kumar).
Is he a judicial officer?
yes
Follow Delhi Judicial Service Assn: tell the District Judge / HC, formal arrest, no handcuffs.
Is she a woman, and is it after sunset?
yes
Only in exceptional cases with prior JMFC permission, by a woman officer (S.43(5)).
routes.end: Arrest without warrant (S.35) — then grounds, relative, lawyer, medical, 24 hours ✓

routes.title: Bail or jail?
steps: Is the offence bailable?
yes
Bail is a right — police or court must release (S.478); personal bond if poor.
Not arrested yet, but fears arrest?
yes
Anticipatory bail from Sessions / HC (S.482) — not for rape of a girl under 16.
Punishable with death or life, with reasonable grounds of guilt?
yes
No Magistrate bail — unless woman, under 16, sick or infirm (S.480 proviso); Sessions / HC may (S.483).
Did he misuse liberty — new offence, threats, absconding?
yes
Cancel bail (S.480(5) / 483(3)) — Dolat Ram.

routes.title: Can he be tried again?
steps: Did a competent court end the earlier case in conviction or acquittal?
no
A discharge or a trial without jurisdiction is no bar — he can be tried.
Is the new charge the same offence, or on the same facts (S.244)?
no
A distinct offence may be tried (S.337(2), with State consent).
Did new consequences happen later (victim died after a hurt conviction)?
yes
May be tried for the graver offence (S.337(3)).
routes.end: Barred — autrefois acquit / convict (S.337, Art. 20(2)); the State must appeal instead ✗

routes.title: The police won’t act
steps: Is the offence cognizable?
no
Police record it (S.174) and send you to the Magistrate — file a complaint (S.223).
Did the SHO refuse to register the FIR?
yes
Send it in writing to the SP (S.173(4)) — registration is mandatory (Lalita Kumari).
Is the investigation stalled or unfair?
yes
Apply to the Magistrate (S.175(3)) — Sakiri Vasu; or file a private complaint (S.223).
routes.end: Still stuck → writ to the High Court for fair investigation / transfer ✓

routes.title: Child accused — which court, what result?
steps: Was he 18 or above on the date of the offence?
yes
Not a child — the regular criminal court.
Was he under 7?
yes
No offence at all (BNS S.20); CWC may give care.
Was he 7–12 and not mature enough to understand?
yes
No offence (BNS S.21).
Heinous offence and aged 16–18?
no
JJB inquiry → reformative orders only (S.18) — special home max 3 years.
routes.end: JJB preliminary assessment (S.15) → Children’s Court may try as adult; no death, no life without release (S.21) ✓

routes.title: Probation or prison?
steps: Is the offence punishable with death or life?
yes
No probation (PO Act S.4; BNSS S.401) — sentence follows.
Theft / cheating or an offence up to 2 years, by a first offender?
yes
Release after admonition (PO Act S.3).
Is the offender under 21?
yes
No imprisonment unless the court records reasons (S.6) — get the probation officer’s report.
routes.end: Release on probation of good conduct — bond up to 3 years, under supervision (S.4) ✓
